items.title: AI for Rakyat programme to equip 100,000 youths with AI tools
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Youths aged between 18 and 30 will be eligible for three months of free access to selected artificial intelligence (AI) tools after completing six modules under the new AI for Rakyat programme. "The six modules are AI Nation 2030: Madani Approach, Cybersafe for Rakyat, Generative AI, AI Safety, Agentic AI for All and Cloud for Rakyat. "Participants who successfully complete all six modules will receive three months of free access to selected AI applications and software.

items.title: Mat Sabu urges more Bumiputera farmers to go big in commercial agriculture
items.summary: SERDANG: Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu wants more Bumiputera farmers to compete in large-scale agriculture, encouraged by the growing number of young people taking up farming full-time. "We hope the younger generation will take up agriculture full-time," he said at the launch of new pomelo and sweet potato varieties at Maha 2026 here today. Mohamad said Bumiputera farmers should compete with communities already established in commercial agriculture.

items.title: Langkawi ferry operators urge urgent dredging of Kuala Kedah, Kuala Perlis lanes
items.summary: ALOR SETAR: Langkawi ferry operators are appealing to the federal government to expedite dredging works in the shipping lanes at Kuala Kedah and Kuala Perlis, where silt deposits are affecting navigational safety. Ferry Line Ventures Sdn Bhd operations manager Lieutenant Commander (Retired) Norhafiz Abdul Wahid said increasingly shallow shipping lanes not only increased the risk to passenger ferry operations but could also cause schedule disruptions and travel delays. Norhafiz said comprehensive and periodic dredging works were needed to ensure the shipping routes remained safe, while allowing ferry operations to run smoothly and accommodate increased passenger numbers.

items.title: Anwar: Malaysia's economic strength shines amid geopolitical uncertainty
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia's six per cent gross domestic product (GDP) growth in the second quarter of this year marks a new chapter in the country's journey towards greater progress and prosperity. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the achievement was particularly encouraging as it came amid an uncertain geopolitical environment, especially the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. No one.

items.title: Anwar: Economic growth benefits must be shared fairly among Malaysians
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The government must ensure that the benefits of Malaysia's economic growth are shared fairly among all segments of society, regardless of race, religion, region or background, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. He said the Madani government faced the challenge of balancing the needs of different groups, including the M40 and B40, Malay and Bumiputera communities, minorities, Sabah and Sarawak, as well as youths, women, persons with disabilities and workers in various sectors. Anwar also said the government must take into account the needs of young people, workers, women, farmers, fishermen, hawkers and gig workers.

items.title: Anwar pledges billions in seized funds for health, education; eases rules for small businesses
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 30 — The government will channel billions of ringgit seized from illegal activities into public healthcare and education, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today, leading a series of fiscal announcements he said were aimed at supporting low-income groups and small businesses. As part of broader relief measures, Anwar also announced a new RM200 million grant scheme under the Geran Sejahtera Madani programme to assist hawkers, small traders, night market vendors, and mothers working from home. The new threshold was among the list of measures Anwar said would provide "temporary relief" as his government aims to alleviate living cost pressure and help businesses.

items.title: Kelantan Umno leaders to attend Pas muktamar, says Takiyuddin
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Umno secretary-general and Kelantan Umno leaders, including the state liaison chairman and division chiefs, have confirmed their attendance at the Pas muktamar. "The confirmed attendees are the Umno secretary-general and Umno leaders in Kelantan, including the state liaison chairman and division chiefs. "Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh will attend the Youth muktamar.

items.title: Communications Ministry to step up efforts to spread information on government assistance
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Communications Ministry will step up efforts to ensure Malaysians are better informed about government assistance, initiatives and achievements. Its minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the ministry would help communicate the various measures announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, including financial assistance and fuel subsidies, and ensure the information reached the public effectively. Fahmi said his ministry would also communicate other measures announced during the address, including the decision to raise the e-Invoice exemption threshold from RM1 million to RM3 million.

items.title: Firefighter's brother to join Smart mission in Nepal to search for missing sibling
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The brother of Malaysian firefighter Mohd Fakhrul Munir, who remains uncontactable in Nepal, will join the Malaysian Special Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) mission to the country following the disaster in Rasuwa. Mohd Saiful Munir Mohd Isa, 46, said he would join the rescue mission as a member of the team while also hoping to obtain news on the whereabouts and condition of his 44-year-old younger brother, known as 'Loe'. Saiful said he hoped his presence in Nepal would enable him to contribute to the rescue mission while providing some relief to the family, which is still waiting for news of Mohd Fakhrul.

items.title: Family unaware three children remained inside house during fire
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The family of three children who were killed in a fire at Kampung Lok Buta, Numbak, early today did not realise that they were still in the house when the incident occurred. M Nasir Jalani, 68, the grandfather of the three victims, said he woke up after hearing one of his children screaming that their neighbour's house was on fire. I ran back into the house, but the children were not there.

items.title: Amirudin says Pakatan prepared for all scenarios, including solo Melaka fight if BN deal fails
items.summary: GOMBAK, Aug 30 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is always prepared for any eventuality in the Melaka state election, including contesting on its own should negotiations on cooperation with Barisan Nasional (BN) fail to reach an agreement. PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said, however, that sufficient room should be given to the party leadership to assess the best strategic options before any decision is finalised. He said the country’s political landscape remained dynamic and flexible, allowing each party room to determine its own approach in facing the election.

items.title: Sarawak Rivers Board warns Rajang journeys perilous as haze blinds boatmen, drought shrinks channels
items.summary: SIBU, Aug 30 — River transport users in Sarawak have been advised to plan their journeys carefully and exercise greater vigilance amid the current drought and haze conditions to avoid untoward incidents. Sarawak Rivers Board (LSS) chairman Dr Safiee Ahmad said the drought had caused river levels to fall, making navigation channels shallower and narrower, while haze had reduced visibility. He said river transport users could also obtain the latest information on river water levels and advisory services from regional LSS offices to help them plan safe journeys.

items.title: Orangutan rescued from fire zone in Indonesia's Borneo, battles respiratory illness
items.summary: KETAPANG, Indonesia: On Sunday morning, Jais, a farmer in Ketapang, West Kalimantan on Borneo island - the province hardest-hit by raging forest fires - was en route to his farm when he found an orangutan writhing on the ground in a weak state on a palm-oil plantation near the fire site. After finding the orangutan, Jais and other residents immediately called for help. Foundation CEO Karmele Llano Sanchez said the orangutan fainted because it did not get enough oxygen.

items.title: Debt dispute sparks armed George Town school fight, police arrest 13 suspects including minors
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 30 — Police have arrested 13 male suspects, including three minors, to assist in investigations into a violent brawl involving weapons that occurred in front of Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Cina (SJKC) Kong Min branch in Air Itam here early yesterday. Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim said all the suspects, aged between 16 and 33, were arrested in five raids across the state through an operation conducted by the Criminal Investigation Department’s Vice, Gambling and Secret Societies Division (D7) of the Penang Police Headquarters, together with the Northeast District Police Headquarters Criminal Investigation Division and with assistance from the Central Police Station. Lim said police were also investigating a vehicle that allegedly struck one of the victims during the brawl, inflicting injuries.

items.title: Anwar unveils six measures to ease cost-of-living pressures in National Day Eve address
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has announced six immediate measures to ease cost-of-living pressures, support businesses and strengthen public services ahead of the tabling of 2027 Budget in October. Anwar said the government decided to introduce the measures now instead of waiting for the Budget as Malaysians and businesses were facing immediate challenges. Anwar said the additional allocation would cover national schools, Chinese and Tamil vernacular schools, religious schools, tahfiz institutions, pondok schools and special education facilities.

items.title: Deputy minister presses Wisma Putra for hotline, briefings as 91 Malaysians missing in Nepal‑China
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 30 — Wisma Putra has been urged to establish a dedicated one-stop centre to provide direct, regular and consistent updates to the next of kin of 91 Malaysians who remain uncontactable following the disaster at the Nepal-China border. Deputy National Unity Minister R. Yuneswaran said the centre should be equipped with a 24-hour hotline, case reference numbers and officers who could be contacted at any time. He said coordination between Wisma Putra, the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), JBPM, Nepalese and Chinese authorities, travel agencies and telecommunications companies must be intensified to verify travel manifests, passport numbers, travel routes and the last known locations of the individuals.

items.title: Next of kin of missing Malaysians in Nepal told to prepare for DNA tests
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The next of kin of Malaysians who have yet to be traced following flash floods and landslides in Nepal have been asked to prepare to undergo deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) tests to assist in the identification process. Sivakumar Kalimuthu, 57, who is still awaiting news of his wife, Kalai Mathe Karuppaiah, 57, said he and his family were informed of the need to undergo the test during a briefing session with the Foreign Ministry at Wisma Putra today. Recalling his last communication with his wife, a housewife, Sivakumar said he received a call from Kalai Mathe at about 11am last Tuesday.

items.title: C4 calls for audit department review after RM4.8bil TH discrepancy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: An anti-graft watchdog has called for a review of the National Audit Department after a RM4.8 billion discrepancy emerged between the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) and the department's report on the fund's finances. "It calls into question how many cases of financial mismanagement in other statutory bodies have yet to be uncovered," he said. Arief said an urgent review of the department's audit practices and governance structure was needed to ensure its audits accurately reflected the financial position of statutory bodies.

items.title: Two-hectare forested area in Taman Bukit Serdang catches fire
items.summary: SERDANG: A two-hectare forested area in Taman Bukit Serdang caught fire today, with firefighters managing to contain the blaze. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the fire was brought under control after firebreaks were established to prevent it from spreading to nearby areas. "The fire involved secondary hill forest, lalang-covered areas and small patches of forest.

items.title: [UPDATED] Anwar: Billions seized from illegal activities to fund education, healthcare
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Billions of ringgit seized from the proceeds of illegal activities through legal proceedings and court decisions will be channelled back to the people, particularly for education and healthcare, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar said the move was part of the government's commitment to ensuring recovered proceeds from wrongdoing ultimately benefited the public. he said.

items.title: Budi95 quota restored to 300 litres, Anwar announces goodies ahead of Merdeka celebration
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 30 — The monthly quota for petrol and diesel subsidies will be raised again, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim revealed today as he announced several goodies ahead of tomorrow’s Merdeka Day celebration. For diesel, the quota would be raised from 300 to 400 litres a month. Anwar said the programme would benefit 16 million people.

items.title: [UPDATED] Budi95 quota restored to 300 litres, diesel allocation raised from Sept 1[WATCH]
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The government will restore the monthly Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) subsidised petrol quota from 200 to 300 litres, benefiting more than 16 million users, effective Sept 1. Anwar said the revised entitlement meant more than 16 million users would be able to purchase up to 300 litres of subsidised RON95 each month. He also announced that more than 500,000 eligible owners of diesel vehicles, including four-wheel-drive vehicles and pick-ups, would receive Budi Diesel assistance of up to 400 litres a month.

items.title: Melaka’s Ab Rauf to steer BN–Pakatan talks, Zahid says timing depends on dissolution
items.summary: SERDANG, Aug 30 — Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi says formal negotiations with Pakatan Harapan (PH) on possible cooperation for the Melaka state election will begin only after the state assembly is dissolved. “We are handing this to Datuk Seri Ab Rauf, and I believe he will hold formal discussions once the Melaka assembly is dissolved,” Zahid told BH. Separately, PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the coalition was waiting for Ab Rauf to indicate his readiness before negotiations could begin.

items.title: 13 hotspots detected in Malaysia as Indonesian fires worsen haze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Thirteen hotspots were detected across Malaysia on Aug 29, as nearly 1,200 hotspots burned in Kalimantan and smoke from Indonesian fires continued to worsen haze conditions across the region. Widespread hotspots were recorded in Kalimantan, while isolated hotspots were detected in Sulawesi, southern and central Sumatra, central Sarawak and East Java. Moderate to dense haze was also observed across most of Kalimantan, central Sarawak, and central and southern Sumatra.

items.title: Technician held for throwing stone at vehicle after road dispute on highway [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A man in his 30s was arrested by police after allegedly throwing a stone at a vehicle on the Kuala Lumpur-Seremban Expressway in Sungai Besi yesterday. Cheras district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Rosdi Daud said the suspect, who works as a technician, was arrested by the roadside along Jalan Suasa 3, Sungai Besi, about 1.15am today. Rosdi said the police had obtained a three-day remand order from the magistrate's court against the suspect, starting today until Sept 1, to assist in investigations.

items.title: Three‑year‑old’s gold necklace snatched at Nilai food festival, police probe RM2,900 theft
items.summary: NILAI, Aug 30 — A woman lost RM2,900 when her three‑year‑old daughter’s gold necklace was snatched while they were strolling at a food festival in N9 Arena here last night. According to Berita Harian (BH), Nilai district police chief Superintendent Johari Yahya said the incident occurred at about 9.30pm when the girl told her mother her necklace was gone. Johari said the mother immediately checked and realised the gold chain was missing.

items.title: Middle East conflict weighs on Wasco earnings outlook
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Research firms have lowered their earnings forecast for Wasco Bhd, citing supply chain disruptions arising from the ongoing conflict in the Middle East that are expected to weigh on the company's operations. RHB Research trimmed its earnings forecasts for the company by 53 per cent, 37 per cent and 17 per cent for financial year 2026 (FY26), FY27 and FY28, respectively, to reflect weaker near-term project execution. RHB Research said that Wasco's core earnings of RM23.8 million for 1H FY26 came below expectations at 24 per cent of the firm's estimates and accounted for 27 per cent of the consensus' forecast.

items.title: SunCon poised to surpass RM8 billion contract wins, says HLIB
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sunway Construction Group Bhd (SunCon) is likely to win more than RM8 billion in new contracts for financial year 2026 (FY26), with year-to-date wins already totalling RM6.9 billion, said Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB). The research house said the latest wins have lifted SunCon's unbilled order book to a record RM10.5 billion as at June 2026, about twice the amount of its FY25 revenue. HLIB added that SunCon could also benefit from its parent company Sunway Bhd's project pipeline, including rapid transit system transport-oriented development works and Seremban hospital works, in our view," it added.

items.title: OCK set for earnings lift from RM500mil diigital pipeline
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: OCK Group Bhd is likely to see stronger earnings going forward on the back of its growing digital infrastructure tenderbook, said RHB Research. Revenue rose 24.2 per cent year-on-year (YoY) to RM229 million from RM184.4 million, while pre-tax profit surged 135.9 per cent to RM36.1 million from RM15.3 million. Net profit jumped 218.1 per cent to RM23.6 million from RM7.4 million, while profit after tax attributable to minority interests soared 384.6 per cent to RM19.4 million from RM4 million.

items.title: Chow: Merdeka is a responsibility to preserve peace, harmony
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang will continue supporting the Madani Government's agenda while ensuring the state's development benefits all communities, said Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow. Chow said Penang's economic progress must go hand in hand with efforts to strengthen social harmony and improve the people's quality of life. He said Penang would remain committed to the Malaysia Madani agenda, particularly in ensuring the state's development continued without neglecting the people's socioeconomic wellbeing.

items.title: Haze: Experts urge public to monitor API, take health precautions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The public should monitor daily Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and take appropriate precautions to reduce health risks during the current haze, according to health experts. Universiti Sultan Zainal Abidin (UniSZA) Faculty of Health Sciences lecturer Dr Anas Ahmad Jamhari said people should check the daily API readings issued by the Department of Environment (DOE) before engaging in outdoor activities, particularly when readings exceed 100. He said those who had to leave home for essential purposes should wear an N95 mask correctly and ensure a proper seal to filter fine PM2.5 particles.

items.title: 15 friends build Twin Towers replica from 2,000 bottles for National Day
items.summary: KOTA BARU: A dream of seeing the Petronas Twin Towers up close has taken an unexpected turn, inspiring 15 friends to build a six-metre-high replica from more than 2,000 discarded plastic bottles. Mohamad Zul Ikwan Azhar, 28, said the project was inspired by his dream of seeing the KLCC towers up close. Zul Ikwan said the group spent about RM3,000 on the project, while the plastic bottles used to construct the tower were bought from a nearby recycle centre.

items.title: Two relief centres opened after Kota Kinabalu fire tragedy leaves 200 victims homeless
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 30 — Two temporary relief centres have been opened at Dewan Kampung Likas and Dewan Damai to shelter more than 200 victims of a fire that broke out in Kampung Lok Buta, Numbak here early this morning. He said the Kota Kinabalu City Hall (DBKK) had declared the area a disaster zone following the incident. Joining Mustapha during the visit was DBKK mayor and District Disaster Management Committee chairman Datuk Seri Dr Sabin Samitah.

items.title: Raja Muda of Perlis proposes three thrusts to guide Mara's future
items.summary: KANGAR: The Raja Muda of Perlis Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra Jamalullail today proposed three main thrusts to guide Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) personnel in steering the agency towards the future. His Royal Highness said the first thrust was for Mara personnel to be bold in exploring and leveraging new technologies, particularly artificial intelligence (AI), to enhance efficiency, creativity and problem-solving capabilities. Mara director-general Datuk Seri Zulfikri Osman was also present.

items.title: Zahid: Cloud seeding targets haze‑hit areas and dams with falling water levels
items.summary: SERDANG, Aug 30 — Cloud seeding operations are being carried out in haze-affected areas, particularly those recording Air Pollutant Index (API) readings above 150, as well as in areas where dams are experiencing falling water levels. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the operations were being carried out in collaboration with the Malaysian Meteorological Department (METMalaysia) and the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF). Three areas in Sarawak recorded hazardous API readings as at 12.30pm today.

items.title: Understanding, kindness key to strengthening national unity, says Loke
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: National unity begins with a conscious effort to understand one another, turning differences into sources of strength and enrichment rather than barriers, Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said. When there is understanding, differences no longer need to become barriers. Loke said diversity could only become an asset when accompanied by goodwill and respect among communities.

items.title: Haze: Public urged to reduce outdoor activities in Sarawak
items.summary: KUCHING: The public, particularly parents, have been urged to avoid outdoor physical activities during the school holidays to protect their children's health amid deteriorating air quality caused by transboundary haze. Sarawak Deputy Minister for Urban Planning, Land Administration and Environment Datuk Len Talif Salleh said precautionary and early preventive measures should be taken, particularly by high-risk groups such as children, the elderly and people with chronic illnesses and respiratory problems. Air quality in several areas in Sarawak deteriorated significantly, with Serian, Samarahan and Kuching recording hazardous API readings as of 12.30pm today.

items.title: Venezuela says retains 'sovereignty' in US oil deal
items.summary: CARACAS: Interim leader Delcy Rodriguez assured the public Saturday that Venezuela retains control of its oil under a new agreement that allows the United States significant access to it. The United States will have majority control of 65 billion barrels of Venezuela's proven reserves in what President Donald Trump described Friday as "the biggest oil deal in world history". "One thing must be absolutely clear: Venezuela retains ownership and sovereignty over its resources," Rodriguez said in a speech on state television.

items.title: Drug offences primary hub driving systemic crime nationwide, says AADK
items.summary: He said national statistics on drug addicts and abusers recorded 123,139 people in 2021, before rising to 137,176 in 2022 and 145,526 in 2023. He said the figure surged to 192,857 people in 2024 before recording a slight decline to 191,832 last year. For Sabah, Ruslin said five-year records showed 6,377 people involved in drug abuse in 2021, 8,156 in 2022, 8,567 in 2023, 9,207 in 2024 and 8,665 last year.

items.title: South Korea names veteran technocrat Lee Hyoung-il as new finance chief in cabinet reshuffle
items.summary: SEOUL: South Korea unveiled a major cabinet reshuffle on Sunday, naming First Vice Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il as the new deputy prime minister and minister of economy and finance. The administration also tapped ruling Democratic Party lawmaker Kim Seung-won to lead the Ministry of Justice, and named Kang Shin-chul, former deputy commander of the South Korea-U.S. Combined Forces Command, as the new defense minister, presidential chief of staff Kang Hoon-sik said in a televised address.

items.title: PM: Malaysia sends SMART team to locate missing citizens in Nepal, commits US$1m aid
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the National Security Council (MKN) and the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA), in collaboration with the Foreign Ministry, have been tasked with coordinating with the Nepalese government to facilitate the deployment of the team as soon as possible. Anwar said Malaysia would also contribute US$1 million (RM4.03 million) to Nepal to assist those affected and support post-disaster recovery efforts. — Bernama Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the National Security Council and the National Disaster Management Agency, in collaboration with the Foreign Ministry, have been tasked with coordinating with the Nepalese government to facilitate the deployment of the team as soon as possible.

items.title: DOE: Transboundary haze thickens 1,211 hotspots detected in southern Asean, mostly in Kalimantan
items.summary: “Widespread hotspots were detected in Kalimantan, while isolated hotspots were recorded in Sulawesi and southern and central Sumatra. Moderate to thick haze was also observed across much of Kalimantan, central Sarawak, and central and southern Sumatra. Azuri Azizah said several air quality monitoring stations in West Kalimantan, western and central Sarawak, western Peninsular Malaysia, and southern and central Sumatra recorded unhealthy to hazardous air quality levels.

items.title: Haze worsens as Serian hits 412, while Samarahan and Kuching record hazardous API levels
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 30 — Serian, Samarahan and Kuching recorded hazardous-level Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 12.30pm today. Sri Aman, meanwhile, recorded a very unhealthy API reading of 228. Areas recording unhealthy API readings include Sarikei (197), Sibu (190), Bintulu (183), Mukah (176), Samalaju (175), Kapit (161), Miri (159) and the the Miri Industrial Training Institute (ILP) (156).

items.title: Govt explores Melaka as alternative venue for LIMA, says Khaled Nordin
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 30 — The government is exploring the possibility of holding the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (LIMA) in Melaka in the future, said Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin. He said, however, that substantial government investment would be needed to ensure the necessary infrastructure was adequately developed before the exhibition could be held in Melaka. So, this is an alternative that we can explore, although as Datuk Rauf (Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh) said, it would require very substantial investment,” he said.

items.title: Fatimah orders agencies to ensure welfare support for family in Sibu child death
items.summary: SIBU, Aug 30 — Sarawak Women, Children and Community Wellbeing Minister Datuk Seri Fatimah Abdullah will instruct the Social Welfare Department (JKM) and Early Childhood Development Division (BPAK) to closely monitor developments in the case of a boy who is believed to have been slashed to death here last Friday. She said this was to ensure that the family affected by the tragedy received appropriate welfare support and psychosocial assistance. “My condolences go out to the victim’s family.

items.title: Melaka PKR plans early candidate announcements, Adam Adli says new faces need preparation
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 30 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) Melaka plans to announce its candidates for the upcoming state election earlier to give its new faces sufficient time to be fully prepared before facing voters. Acting chairman of the Melaka PKR Leadership Council Adam Adli Abdul Halim said the candidate selection process is undergoing several stages of screening, starting at the branch and state levels, before being submitted to the central level to be finalised by the party president. He said the Melaka PKR would also strengthen its election machinery through a series of launches in Tangga Batu, Hang Tuah Jaya, Alor Gajah, Masjid Tanah and Jasin.

items.title: Senator says RCI vital to clarify Tabung Haji losses, systemic flaws demand scrutiny
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 30 — The Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) was crucial to determine whether Lembaga Tabung Haji’s (TH) investment losses stemmed from weaknesses in investment decision-making or other factors, said Senator Muhammad Hasbi Muda. He said while losses were a normal part of investment activities and did not necessarily indicate criminal wrongdoing, the issues involving TH warranted a comprehensive examination given the number of troubled investments highlighted. That was why we need the RCI,” he said.

items.title: Malaysia King expresses hope for smooth National Day celebrations after audience with PM Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 30 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, has expressed hope that tomorrow’s National Day celebrations will run smoothly, with all parties involved doing their utmost to ensure their success. According to a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar’s Facebook page today, His Majesty said this after granting an audience to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim at Istana Bukit Tunku here. Sultan Ibrahim and Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, are scheduled to attend the celebrations, along with Anwar and members of the Cabinet.

items.title: Three Malaysians among 261 foreign nationals unaccounted for after Gyirong mudslide at China‑Nepal border
items.summary: GYIRONG (China), Aug 30 — Three Malaysians are among 261 foreign nationals from 23 countries identified as unaccounted for following a mudslide that struck Gyirong Port along the China-Nepal border in southwest China’s Xizang Autonomous Region on Aug 26, local authorities said Sunday. The latest figure was announced at a press conference held by the regional government’s information office following a joint search and cross-checking of information by foreign affairs, public security, culture and tourism, and emergency management authorities, Xinhua reported. Chinese authorities have notified the countries' embassies and consulates in China, according to the press conference.

items.title: Police probe viral video of headscarves with incomplete Jalur Gemilang patterns in Subang Jaya
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 30 — Police are investigating a video clip that has gone viral depicting the sale of headscarves, allegedly featuring incomplete Jalur Gemilang patterns, at a supermarket in Subang Jaya, Selangor. Subang Jaya police chief ACP Wan Azlan Wan Mamat said they received a report regarding the matter at about 4.49pm yesterday. Wan Azlan said that following the circulation of the video, police were conducting investigations under.

items.title: Three children killed as massive Kota Kinabalu fire razes over 200 squatter houses
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 30 — Three children were killed in a fire that swept through more than 200 houses in three villages here early this morning. The Sabah Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) said in a statement that the victims were identified as Nana Abdullah, four; Mohd Asrul Abdullah, six; and Nurfarahdilah Mohd Tajihah, eight. According to JBPM, the fire involved non-permanent stilt houses in a squatter settlement across three villages, namely Kampung Lok Buta, Kampung Lok Poring and Kampung Sabang Lama.

items.title: Police confirm drowning after Kenyir boat hits tree stump, victim trapped beneath overturned vessel
items.summary: KUALA BERANG, Aug 30 — An elderly woman died after the boat she was travelling in hit a tree stump before capsizing around Gua Bewah, Tasik Kenyir in Hulu Terengganu yesterday. Hulu Terengganu police chief Supt Sharudin Abdul Wahab said initial investigations found that the victim, who was from Felda Chiku in Kelantan, had come to Tasik Kenyir for a holiday on a houseboat with 27 family members. “At 11am yesterday, the victim, 63-year-old Wan Esah Wan Daud and three other family members boarded a houseboat from Tasik Kenyir heading towards Taman Negara.

items.title: Farres Putra dies after Cub Prix crash, Kuala Terengganu police confirm multiple injuries
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 30 — A post-mortem has confirmed that multiple injuries sustained in a crash during the Malaysian Cub Prix Championship were the cause of death of CKJ Racing rider Farres Putra Mohd Fadhill, 18, yesterday. Kuala Terengganu police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said the post-mortem was conducted at the Forensic Department of Sultanah Nur Zahirah Hospital (HSNZ) from 10pm to 11.55pm yesterday. Meanwhile, Farres’ friend Adi Putra Anahar, 17, said he was in a car watching the race live on his smartphone when the broadcast suddenly ended.

items.title: Nepal floods leave 55 Malaysians uncontactable, 36 more missing in China, says ministry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 30 — A total of 91 Malaysians, comprising 55 in Nepal and 36 in China, remain reported as uncontactable as of 8pm on Saturday following the floods that struck on Aug 26, the Foreign Ministry said. “The Ministry understands the heightened concern regarding the limited personal information released publicly on individual Malaysians who remain uncontactable,” it said on Saturday. Consular officers have contacted all verified immediate next of kin whose details are available to provide updates on current developments.

items.title: Foreign minister says briefing today for families of Malaysians missing in Nepal floods
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 30 — A briefing will be held today with the families of Malaysians still unaccounted for following severe flash floods and landslides in Nepal’s Rasuwa district. Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said the briefing will involve Wisma Putra, the National Security Council and relevant agencies to provide an update on efforts to locate those reported missing. Mohamad said the ministry’s operations room is operating round the clock to monitor developments involving Malaysians affected by the disaster, with Wisma Putra maintaining close communication with Nepal’s Foreign Ministry and relevant agencies for updates.

items.title: Serian tops hazardous API chart at 364, multiple Sarawak districts suffer worsening air
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 30 — Serian recorded a hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) reading as of 8am today. Meanwhile, three areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy API readings, namely Samarahan (300), Kuching (291) and Sri Aman (214). Meanwhile, five areas in the peninsula, namely Kuala Lumpur, Selangor and Perak recorded unhealthy API readings as of 9am today.

items.title: Early morning fire in Kota Kinabalu squatter area, 39 personnel deployed to contain blaze
items.summary: The Sabah Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), in a statement, said it received an emergency call at 1.40am, following which firefighters were deployed and arrived at the scene, located 18 kilometres away, at 1.58am. “A total of 39 personnel from the Kota Kinabalu, Lintas and Penampang Fire and Rescue Stations (BBP) were deployed to the scene to carry out firefighting operations,” it said. According to the Sabah JBPM, firefighters were battling the blaze using two streams and four water jets, with water supplied by fire engines.

items.title: Beyond monuments and textbooks, KL’s Statesman Memorial guards Malaysia’s nation‑building story
items.summary: One such place is the Statesman Memorial (also known as Memorial Negarawan), housed in the former Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) along Jalan Dato Onn, which bears witness to the country’s post-independence administrative history. National Archives of Malaysia (ANM) director-general Zaidin Mohd Noor said the building’s historical significance lies not merely in its role as an administrative office, but as a physical witness to Malaysia’s journey in governance and development. — Picture by Yusof Isa The former Prime Minister’s Office housed the tenures of Tun Abdul Razak Hussein, Tun Hussein Onn and Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad — who occupied the office for the longest period, 22 years — until the federal government administrative centre moved to Putrajaya in 2003.

items.title: As cyber threats strike at AI speed, Malaysia urged to embed risk‑based defence
items.summary: Telekom Malaysia Chief Information Security Officer Raja Azrina Raja Othman, who was among the co-founders of MyCERT in 1997, said cyber threats three decades ago were largely confined to specific systems and networks. Today, however, almost all services operate digitally and are interconnected, ranging from banking and government services to corporate operations and national critical infrastructure. “Cyber attackers today operate rapidly with the aid of AI.

items.title: Immigration to seek Thai details on syndicate trafficking China nationals from Cambodia into Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — The Immigration Department will work with Thai authorities to obtain detailed information on an alleged syndicate trafficking China nationals from Cambodia to Malaysia. “We will get further information from Thai authorities on this matter,” he said when contacted by Bernama today, after Thai media outlets reported that Thai authorities arrested two individuals suspected of being masterminds of a ring trafficking China nationals from the Cambodian border to Malaysia through Thailand. Thai authorities also identified four Thai nationals believed to be involved in the ring, including the individual arranging the immigrants’ journey from the Cambodia-Thai border to Hat Yai and onwards through to Malaysia.
